title: Links, images, and media
summary: Use anchors, images with alt text, and responsive media elements correctly.

scenario.briefing: The storefront has placeholder links, images without descriptions, and a video that autoplays with sound. Fix the markup so links point to real destinations, images describe themselves, and media does not interrupt visitors.

objectives.description: Use meaningful anchor text and destinations.
Provide alt text and accessible media.
Transfer link and media decisions to a new page.

hints: Anchor text should describe the destination.
Images need alt text; decorative ones use empty alt.
Avoid autoplay with sound; provide controls.
Use href with real paths, alt on images, and controls on video without autoplay.

misconceptions.testDescription: Links use descriptive text instead of 'click here'.
misconceptions.feedback: Link text should describe the destination. 'Click here' is meaningless out of context and hard to scan.

misconceptions.description: Autoplaying media with sound is acceptable by default.
misconceptions.feedback: Autoplay with sound interrupts visitors and can violate accessibility expectations. Provide controls and avoid sound by default.

sections.title: Links name destinations
sections.body: Anchor text should describe where the link goes. Screen reader users often navigate by a list of links, so 'click here' is useless. Use real href values rather than placeholder fragments.

sections.title: Media needs care
sections.body: Images need alternative text unless they are decorative. Video and audio should provide controls and avoid autoplay with sound. Captions help users who cannot hear.

vocabulary.definition: An element that creates a hyperlink.
A text alternative for an image.
